title: tk factory setup credential walkthrough
description: The BotFather-style first-run walk (deployment model section): checks wrangler auth, offers tk factory deploy if no deployment exists, walks the GitHub credential ladder (fine-grained repo-scoped PAT first; personal GitHub App documented as the upgrade path) and stores the choice as Worker secrets, configures the AI Gateway base URL and provider keys (Workers AI needs no key — same account), and verifies each rung with a live probe (a gateway model list call, a GitHub API call with the PAT) before moving on. Mirrors the tone and structure of tk channel setup telegram: one rung at a time, verify, then persist; secrets go to Worker secrets or ~/.ticksrc (0600), never the repo.
notes:
2026-08-19 15:20 - [human] Secrets decision: the credential walkthrough offers Doppler as the storage rung for operator-side credentials (project 'ticks', workplace Engelbrecht) in preference to ~/.ticksrc when the doppler CLI is present and authed; runtime secrets still land as Cloudflare Worker secrets. ~/.ticksrc (0600) stays the no-Doppler fallback.
2026-08-19 16:06 - Credential-rung facts established during this run (orchestrator, 2026-08-19):
1. Doppler is an OPTIONAL rung, never a dependency — see the new .tick/config.md Rule. Offer it when the doppler CLI is present and scoped; otherwise env -> ~/.ticksrc (0600) -> interactive prompt, with no degraded outcome and no error naming a tool the user does not have.
2. Read/write ~/.ticksrc through internal/ticksrc (shipped by 7c1) — it preserves board-sync keys, comments and unknown keys, and enforces 0600. Do not hand-roll file writes.
3. /health returns auth:{required,configured} — the offline-safe probe for 'is the factory token configured', no token needed.
4. wrangler CANNOT mint Cloudflare API tokens (only login/secret/secrets-store). The 'cf' CLI (v0.6.0) CAN: 'cf accounts tokens create' supports --name, --expires-on, --not-before, --condition-request-ip-in/not-in, --dry-run and --body, minting ACCOUNT-OWNED tokens (not user-owned) — scoped to the account, not tied to a person, individually revocable. Bootstrapping it still needs one credential carrying API-Tokens:Edit, which a default cf OAuth profile does NOT have (verified: 87 scopes, zero token-management scopes, 'cf accounts tokens list' -> 403 [9109]).
5. Therefore the credential walk must treat token minting as an OPTIONAL accelerator behind a functional probe ('cf accounts tokens list' succeeds?), never a required step, and must work end to end for an operator who only pastes a token from the dashboard.
